firstSentence: 3D Gaussian splatting is a scene representation of anisotropic 3D Gaussians, each with position, covariance, opacity and view-dependent colour, rasterised onto the image plane instead of ray-marched.
Action chunking is predicting a sequence of future actions in one inference instead of a single action per timestep.
Action tokenization is expressing continuous robot actions as discrete tokens a language model can produce.
Admittance control is compliant control that measures contact force and commands motion in response, the dual of impedance control.
An affordance is an estimate of whether an available skill can succeed now.
An antipodal grasp is a two-contact grasp in which the line through the contact points lies strictly inside both friction cones.
An automated storage and retrieval system is a warehouse subsystem of fixed racking, cranes or shuttles and control software storing and retrieving unit loads without a human walking an aisle.
An autonomous mobile robot is a self-navigating transport vehicle that plans its own paths through a facility with onboard sensors, unlike an automated guided vehicle following fixed tape or wire.
Backdrivability is how easily an external force can move a joint with the actuators passive, and it decides which compliance scheme fits the hardware.
Behavior cloning is supervised learning of a policy from expert demonstrations, with observations as inputs and the expert's actions as labels.
Brownfield deployment is installing automation in an existing, running facility, around its floor plans, ceiling heights, power drops, traffic lanes and a production schedule that cannot simply stop.

Camera intrinsics are the camera's own parameters, independent of where it is mounted: focal length in pixels along each axis, the principal point where the optical axis meets the sensor, and lens distortion.
The committed horizon is the number of predicted actions a system executes before a fresh inference replaces them.
Compounding error is the accumulation of small per-step mistakes in a sequential task.
Configuration space is the space of a robot's configurations, one point per complete joint assignment; a 7-DoF arm moves through a 7-dimensional space with joint angles as coordinates.
Conformal prediction is a distribution-free procedure that turns any model’s raw score into a prediction set with guaranteed coverage.
Contact-rich manipulation is manipulation governed by making, holding and breaking contact: insertion, screwing, wiping, folding.
A control barrier function is a scalar function of the state that is positive on a set the system should stay inside.
A costmap is the grid a mobile-robot navigation stack plans over: map and live sensor occupancy, inflated by the robot's footprint and marked with other route costs.
Covariate shift is the mismatch between the state distribution of an imitation learner's training demonstrations and the distribution its learned policy visits at deployment.
Cross-embodiment learning is learning from, or transferring to, robots with different morphologies: joint counts, action dimensions and sensor suites.
Curriculum learning is training on tasks that start easy and grow harder as the agent improves.
A CVAE (conditional variational autoencoder) is a generative model learning a distribution over a latent variable instead of one deterministic output.
Cycle time is the measured time required to produce a part or complete a process.
DAgger (Dataset Aggregation) is an iterative fix for behavior cloning's distribution mismatch: the expert labels states the current policy visits, and the policy retrains on the aggregate.
Degrees of freedom are the number of independent coordinates needed to specify a mechanism's configuration; an arm has one per independent joint.
Denavit-Hartenberg parameters are a four-parameter representation of a kinematic chain.
A diffusion policy is a policy generating a whole action sequence by conditional denoising diffusion instead of regressing one action.
Distribution shift is the mismatch between a model's training data and its deployment data.
Domain randomization is training a policy across a distribution of simulators with randomized visual appearance, dynamics or both, so the real world reads as one more sample.
An emergency stop is a machine function, started by a single human action, that halts hazardous motion.
An end effector is the last link of a robot arm plus its gripper, hand or tool, whose pose the arm exists to place.
End-to-end driving is a policy mapping raw sensor input directly to a motion plan or vehicle commands, without separate perception, prediction and planning modules.
A factor graph is a bipartite graph of a probability distribution's factorization: variable nodes hold unknown states, factor nodes the measurements and motion constraints linking them.
Flow matching is a generative modeling recipe that learns a time-dependent vector field carrying noise to data, by regressing against the conditional flow instead of estimating a score.
Force closure is the property that a grasp can resist any external wrench with contact forces inside the friction cones.
Force feedback is sensing interaction forces at the instrument tip and rendering them as resistance at the operator's controls.
Form closure is force closure by geometry alone: frictionless contact normals positively span the wrench space, immobilizing the object however small the friction.
Forward kinematics is the map from a robot's joint angles to its end-effector pose, a deterministic composition of per-joint transforms.
A friction cone is the set of forces a frictional point contact can exert without slipping: all forces within arctan(mu) of the surface normal, mu being the Coulomb friction coefficient.
Functional safety is the part of a system’s safety that depends on its control system working correctly, as opposed to inherent design or physical guarding.
Goods-to-person is the warehouse principle of bringing stored items to a stationary picker at a pick station instead of walking the picker to the shelves.
The grasp wrench space is the set of net wrenches a grasp can apply, mapped from admissible contact forces through the grasp map.
Hand-eye calibration is estimating the rigid transform between a camera and the robot frame it reports into.
A hierarchical policy is a control architecture in which a high-level policy chooses what to do next and low-level policies execute it.
Hindsight experience replay (HER) is an off-policy technique that replays stored transitions with alternative goals and recomputed rewards, alongside original-goal replay.
Hybrid force/position control is Raibert and Craig's split of a contact task into orthogonal subspaces.
Imitation learning is learning a policy from expert demonstrations instead of a reward signal, by supervised fitting of recorded state-action pairs.
Impedance control is Hogan's 1985 formulation of compliant contact control, programming the relationship between position and force instead of commanding either.
In-hand manipulation is repositioning or reorienting a grasped object within the hand without setting it down, like rolling a pen or turning a key.
In-situ resource utilization (ISRU) is producing mission consumables at the destination from local materials instead of launching them from Earth.
Intervention rate is the fraction of cycles in which an automated system needs a human for a jam, mispick or fault, or one minus the per-cycle success rate.
Inverse kinematics is finding joint angles that place the end effector at a target pose, the reverse of forward kinematics.
The Jacobian is the derivative of the forward-kinematics map: a matrix with one column per joint, relating joint velocities to end-effector velocity at the current configuration.
The Kalman filter is the recursive state estimator for linear systems with Gaussian noise.
Knowledge insulation is Physical Intelligence's recipe for protecting a vision-language-action model's pretrained backbone from action learning.
Latent dynamics is a world-model paradigm predicting in a compact learned latent space instead of pixels.
Legged locomotion is moving on legs instead of wheels or tracks, re-establishing balance at every discrete, intermittent foothold with no continuous contact patch.
The long tail is the individually rare, collectively decisive part of the scenario distribution.
Loop closure is recognising a mapped place and adding a validated constraint between observations.
Mean time between failures (MTBF) is a reliability parameter for repairable systems.
A mechanoreceptor is a sensory nerve ending that fires under mechanical stimuli such as pressure, vibration or skin stretch.
Minimally invasive surgery is surgery through small incisions with elongated instruments and a camera, instead of a large open incision.

Model predictive control is constant re-planning against an explicit dynamics model: each step it optimizes a short action sequence, executes only the first action and re-solves from the measured state.
A neural radiance field is a scene stored as a continuous function, a small neural network, from 3D position and viewing direction to volume density and view-dependent colour.
An occupancy grid is a map of cells, each storing the probability that it is occupied.
An off-policy method is a learning method that can improve one policy from data generated by another, so old experience stays usable.
Offline reinforcement learning is learning a policy from a fixed dataset of previously collected transitions, without new environment experience during training.
On-orbit servicing is using one spacecraft to work on another after launch.
An on-policy method is a learning method whose updates are valid only for data from the current policy, so each batch of experience is used once and discarded.
Open X-Embodiment is a 2023 collaboration of 34 labs that pooled 60 existing robot datasets into one standardized format: over a million trajectories from 22 embodiments, covering 527 skills.
An operational design domain (ODD) is the set of conditions an automated driving system is designed for: geography, road types, speed range, weather and time of day.
Out-of-distribution detection is deciding at run time whether a model's input resembles its training data, so a policy can decline instead of extrapolating.
Parallel simulation is running thousands of physics simulator instances at once on one GPU, so one workstation gathers reinforcement learning experience at rates that once needed CPU clusters.
Payback period is the time an automation investment takes to return its cost: total cell capital over its monthly value, most often displaced labour.
A performance level is the ISO 13849-1:2023 counterpart of a safety integrity level, the rating a machinery integrator in Europe most often must meet.
Place recognition is deciding, in visual navigation, whether the current image shows a mapped place.
A point cloud is a set of 3D points, usually with no ordering and no connectivity, as produced by back-projecting depth-camera or lidar measurements through the camera intrinsics.
Pose estimation is recovering an object's full rigid position and orientation, six degrees of freedom, from sensor data.
Power and force limiting is the collaborative mode that permits robot-person contact and makes it safe by bounding what the contact can do.
PPO (proximal policy optimization) is the on-policy reinforcement learning algorithm the locomotion literature standardized on.
The predicted horizon is the chunk length H: the number of future actions a chunked policy emits in one forward pass, whether or not it executes them all.
Promptable segmentation is predicting a mask from an image plus prompts such as foreground/background points, a box or a mask.
Proprioception is sensing the body's own state (joint positions and velocities, orientation, contact), as opposed to exteroception of the outside world through cameras or lidar.
Q-learning is learning a function predicting the return from each state-action pair, instead of a policy directly, then picking the action its own estimate rates highest.
Real-time chunking is an inference-time scheme keeping chunked policies responsive when inference is slower than control.
A replay buffer is the store of past transitions an off-policy learner samples gradient batches from.
Reset-free learning is training on real hardware without a human resetting the scene between attempts.
Retargeting is mapping motion recorded on one body, usually a human's, onto a robot with different proportions and joint limits, so human demonstrations become references the robot can track.
Reward shaping is adding rewards to a task's base reward to guide learning, usually densifying a sparse success signal.
Risk assessment is the documented machinery-safety procedure for finding a machine's hazards and judging their risks.
A robotic assisted surgical device (RASD) is the US regulatory category for surgical robots, cleared or authorized to assist a surgeon, who remains the one practicing medicine.
A safety case is a structured, documented argument, with evidence for each step, that a system is acceptably safe for a given application and environment.
A safety integrity level is the IEC 61508:2010 confidence rating for a safety function; it belongs to the function, whichever component implements it.
Sample efficiency is how much environment interaction a method needs to reach a set performance, counted apart from wall-clock time and gradient updates.
A scaling law is an empirical relation between performance and resources (parameters, data or compute), first made precise for language models and now measured in robot learning.
Semantic segmentation is labelling every pixel of an image with a class, instead of boxing each object.
A series elastic actuator is one with a deliberately soft spring between gear train and load, proposed by Pratt and Williamson in 1995.
A signed-distance field is a scalar field whose zero crossing represents a surface.
The sim-to-real gap is the discrepancy between a simulator's physics and rendering and the real world, which degrades simulation-trained policies on hardware.
SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) is estimating a robot's state while building a model of its environment.
Speed and separation monitoring is the collaborative mode in which robot and person may move simultaneously while a safety system continuously keeps a protective separation distance between them.
Success rate is the fraction of attempted episodes in which a policy completes the task, the standard headline metric of robot learning evaluation.

Swarm robotics is coordinating many relatively simple robots through local interaction, without a central planner, for collective behavior no individual achieves, such as coverage, mapping or search at fleet scale.
Symmetry-aware pose error (ADD-S) is a pose-error rule using nearest-neighbour matches instead of fixed model-point correspondences.
System identification is fitting a simulator's parameters to a real robot's measured dynamics, shrinking the sim-to-real gap by calibration.
A systems integrator is an organisation that integrates a robot with end-effectors, sensors, safeguarding and controls needed for an application.
Tactile sensing is sensing contact through a robot's skin with pressure arrays, barometric cells or optical fingertip cameras.
Takt time is available production time divided by customer demand over the same period, in time per unit.
Teacher-student distillation is training two policies in sequence for partial observability.
Teleoperation is direct remote control of a robot by a human operator, used in robot learning mostly to record expert demonstrations.
Temporal ensembling is ACT's execution scheme for overlapping action chunks: the policy runs every timestep and averages in-flight predictions for the current step with exponential weights.
Trajectory optimization is motion planning by numerically optimizing a candidate trajectory.
A vision-language model is a model pretrained jointly on web-scale image and text data, so visual recognition and language semantics share one set of weights.
A vision-language-action model is a vision-language model, pretrained on web-scale image and text data, adapted to output robot actions.
Visual servoing is controlling a robot's motion with computer vision data.
Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is state estimation for a flying robot fusing camera images with inertial measurement unit data.
Whole-body control is treating all of a robot's actuated degrees of freedom (legs, torso, arms, hands) as one coupled problem instead of an arm controller stacked on a separate locomotion controller.
A world model is a model an agent queries to make decisions: given the current observation or state and a candidate action, it predicts what happens next.
